name: Alice — The Crown of Little Wonders

pages.name: Quick Reference
pages.html:
The Crown does not make Alice's spells hit harder. It makes "what if I try this" into something the rules will actually let her do, and then keeps widening what counts as a reasonable idea.

Wondrous item, legacy item (requires attunement by Alice)

Your Charges

The Wonder Charges pool grows on its own at 6th, 10th and 15th level. You never have to update the sheet — the number just changes.

StateYour levelWonder ChargesBack at dawn
Dormantlevels 3–53all of them
Awakenedlevels 6–95all of them
Exaltedlevels 10–1471d6 + 1
Legendarylevel 15+91d8 + 1

At Dormant and Awakened every spent charge comes back. From 10th level it stops refilling completely: the pool is bigger, and a heavy day stays expensive into the next one.

Legacy Save DC

Where a feature makes something roll a saving throw, the DC is 8 + proficiency bonus + spellcasting ability modifier. It comes off your sheet, so it rises as you do.

What Unlocks When

Features arrive on their own. Below its level a feature is not on the item at all, so anything you can see on the sheet is something you can use. Where a later state improves an earlier feature, the old version disappears and the new one takes its place.

Dormant — levels 3–5 (Uncommon): Borrowed Cantrips; Pocketful of Nonsense; Oops; Little Places.

Awakened — levels 6–9 (Rare): Rabbit Hole; Improvised Solution; That's Mine Now.

Exalted — levels 10–14 (Very Rare): Make-Believe; It Was Worth a Try; Follow the Kender.

Legendary — level 15+ (Legendary): The World Is More Interesting This Way; You Can't Take This From Me; Happily Ever After.

Advancing

Reaching the level makes the next state possible. What actually wakes the item is the moment named at the top of each state below — a choice, not an achievement, and never something you can win in a fight. You do not need to chase it. When it happens, you will know, and so will the item.

pages.name: Levels 3–5 — Dormant
pages.html:
Uncommon · levels 3–5 · 3 Wonder Charges, all of them returning at dawn

Where it starts. This is the item as you first receive it. Everything below is yours from the moment you attune.

Everything from earlier states still works unless a feature here says it replaces one.

Borrowed Cantrips

Passive. Always on. Nothing to click and nothing to spend.

Alice learns druidcraft and minor illusion. They count as sorcerer spells for her and do not count against her cantrips known. If she already knows either, she may replace that cantrip with another non-damaging bard, druid or sorcerer cantrip.

Pocketful of Nonsense

Bonus action — 1 charge

As a bonus action, expend 1 Wonder Charge to produce one effect:

  • Hop. Alice or a willing creature within 30 feet moves up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space Alice can see. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks but cannot pass through solid objects.
  • Fetch. One unattended object Alice can see within 30 feet weighing no more than 10 pounds flies into her hand. An object being worn, carried, secured or magically anchored cannot be affected.
  • Distract. One creature Alice can see within 30 feet has disadvantage on its next opportunity attack or Wisdom (Perception) check before the start of Alice's next turn.

Oops

Reaction — 1 charge

When Alice or a creature she can see within 30 feet makes an ability check, Alice can use her reaction and expend 1 charge to add 1d4 after seeing the roll but before the outcome is declared.

Little Places

Passive. Always on. Nothing to click and nothing to spend.

Alice can move through the space of any creature larger than herself, and squeezing costs her no additional movement.

pages.name: Levels 6–9 — Awakened
pages.html:
Rare · levels 6–9 · 5 Wonder Charges, all of them returning at dawn

What wakes it. Alice openly acknowledges something genuinely important to her rather than hiding it behind humour, bravado or performance, and then acts upon it.

Everything from earlier states still works unless a feature here says it replaces one.

Rabbit Hole

Reaction — 2 charges

When Alice takes damage, she can use her reaction and expend 2 charges to teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space she can see. If this takes her outside the triggering effect's range, it does not prevent the triggering damage. After teleporting, Alice can become invisible until the beginning of her next turn or until she attacks, deals damage or casts a spell.

Improvised Solution

No action — 1 charge · 1× per short or long rest

When Alice attempts an unconventional but physically or magically plausible use of an object, spell or environmental feature, she can expend 1 charge to gain advantage on one associated ability check or spellcasting ability check. If the improvised action instead immediately forces exactly one creature to make a saving throw, Alice can impose disadvantage on that save. Once this feature succeeds, it cannot be used again until she finishes a short or long rest.

That's Mine Now

Action — 1 charge — 10 minutes

Alice can expend 1 charge to cast mage hand, except that the hand can carry 30 pounds, its range is 60 feet, and Alice can make it appear as any Tiny hand, paw, claw or similarly shaped appendage. It lasts 10 minutes and requires no concentration.

pages.name: Levels 10–14 — Exalted
pages.html:
Very Rare · levels 10–14 · 7 Wonder Charges, regaining 1d6 + 1 at dawn rather than all expended charges

What wakes it. Alice deliberately risks something she values because another person's happiness, safety or sense of wonder matters more to her than avoiding hurt herself.

Everything from earlier states still works unless a feature here says it replaces one.

Make-Believe

Action — 3 charges — 10 minutes

As an action, Alice expends 3 charges and describes a mundane object she can see or has personally encountered before. The created object appears in an unoccupied space within 30 feet and lasts 10 minutes, functioning as a normal nonmagical object of its type. It:

  • must fit within a 10-foot cube;
  • can weigh no more than 500 pounds;
  • cannot have a market value above 100 gp;
  • cannot contain poison, explosives, alchemical substances or other consumable compounds;
  • cannot be a spell component with a listed monetary value;
  • cannot be a firearm or siege weapon;
  • cannot duplicate a magic item;
  • cannot be a functioning complex mechanism requiring more than five independently moving components.

A created object cannot be sold and vanishes if broken into separate components. A ladder, rowboat, door, table, bridge section, mattress, cage, giant umbrella, wheelbarrow or ridiculous throne are all fair game.

It Was Worth a Try

No action — 1× per short or long rest

Once per short or long rest, when Alice fails an ability check by 5 or less, she can decide that the attempt succeeds instead — in the messiest reasonable way. The DM may introduce a complication, but the complication cannot negate the success. This is not usable on attack rolls or saving throws.

Follow the Kender

Reaction — 1 charge

When Alice uses Rabbit Hole, she may expend 1 additional charge to take one willing creature within 5 feet with her. Both creatures arrive in unoccupied spaces within 5 feet of one another.

pages.name: Level 15+ — Legendary
pages.html:
Legendary · level 15+ · 9 Wonder Charges, regaining 1d8 + 1 at dawn

What wakes it. Alice willingly chooses genuine belonging despite knowing that loving people gives the world something it can take from her.

Everything from earlier states still works unless a feature here says it replaces one.

The World Is More Interesting This Way

Make-Believe (The World Is More Interesting This Way). Action — 3 charges — 1 hour

Make-Believe improves: the maximum dimensions become a 20-foot cube, the maximum weight becomes 2,000 pounds, the maximum mundane value becomes 500 gp, and the duration becomes 1 hour. Alice can also create a simple structure composed of connected mundane parts, such as a small cottage, bridge, stage, wagon or sailing boat. It still cannot create valuable materials, creatures, food with magical effects, siege weapons, spell components, magic items or advanced machinery.

You Can't Take This From Me

Reaction — 3 charges

When Alice or a creature she can see within 30 feet fails a saving throw against being charmed, frightened, possessed or magically controlled, Alice can use her reaction and expend 3 charges. The creature rerolls the saving throw with advantage. On a success, it also gains immunity to that specific creature's charm, fear, possession and control effects until the next dawn.

Happily Ever After

Reaction — 1× per long rest — temporary hit points equal to twice your sorcerer level

Once per long rest, when Alice or an ally within 30 feet would be reduced to 0 hit points, Alice can declare "That's not how this story ends." The creature instead drops to 1 hit point, immediately gains temporary hit points equal to twice Alice's sorcerer level, and may use its reaction to move up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks. This is not resurrection. Alice cannot stop death forever. She can occasionally insist that this is not the page where it happens.

pages.name: Playing It Well
pages.html:
The Crown does not make Alice's spells hit harder. It makes "what if I try this" into something the rules will actually let her do, and then keeps widening what counts as a reasonable idea.

At the Table

  • Oops works on anybody. It is a reaction on any ability check made by Alice or a creature she can see within 30 feet. One charge to rescue somebody else's failed check is the cheapest good thing the Crown does.
  • Improvised Solution only burns its rest use when it works. A failed improvisation costs the charge and nothing else, so there is no reason not to try.
  • Hop is an escape, not a step. It ignores opportunity attacks, so it pulls an ally out of a bad square without spending their Disengage.
  • From 10th level the Crown stops refilling completely. Two Rabbit Holes in a day is four of seven charges. Past that point plan the day rather than the round.
  • Make-Believe is at its best structurally — a ladder, a bridge section, a door, a cage, a rowboat, a wheelbarrow. Reach for architecture before you reach for objects.

Questions That Come Up

Can Make-Believe create a weapon?
A mundane one under the value cap, yes — it is an ordinary nonmagical object. Not a firearm, not a siege weapon, and never a magic item.

Does Rabbit Hole prevent the damage that triggered it?
No. Explicitly not, even if the teleport carries her out of the effect's range.

Can Follow the Kender carry someone who does not want to go?
No. Willing creatures only.

Does Happily Ever After save someone killed outright?
No. It triggers on being reduced to 0 hit points. An effect that kills outright never produces that moment to catch.

Which ability do the Crown's cantrips use?
They count as sorcerer spells for her, so her sorcerer spellcasting ability.

If Something Here Disagrees With the Item

The item on your sheet is the rules. This journal is generated from the same source, so the two should never differ — but if they do, the item wins and your DM should know.
